decisive_items: ST segments elevated 4-6 mm in leads II, III and aVF, with ST depression in leads V2-V6
Widespread ST-segment elevations (4-15 mm) in leads II, III, aVF, and V2-V6
10% stenosis in proximal left anterior descending artery (LAD) and right coronary artery (RCA)
response.rationale: Transient widespread ST elevations with non-obstructive coronary arteries and alcohol-triggered syncope/arrhythmias favor coronary vasospasm (variant angina) over primary arrhythmia or cardiomyopathy.

rejected.why: AV block is an ECG manifestation, not the underlying cause, and does not explain the ST elevations or alcohol trigger.
Alcohol-induced arrhythmias could explain VT/syncope but not the widespread ST elevations; these arrhythmias are likely secondary to vasospastic ischemia.
Chronic alcohol use is present, but there are no heart failure or cardiomyopathy features, and the ST elevations with non-obstructive coronaries point to spasm.
No structural or echocardiographic evidence of HOCM is provided, and the ST elevations with non-obstructive coronaries are more consistent with vasospasm.
